## Findings
- claim-1: For \(I_{r,n-r}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^r\}\), \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has Schur basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and multiplication is LR multiplication truncated to that box. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: For \(A=\Lambda/I_{6,5}\), \(A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5)\).
- claim-3: In each degree \(d\), the complete Pieri rows \(h_t\bar s_\lambda\), \(1\le t\le5\), with \(22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6\) and \(|\lambda|=d-t\), present \((A_+J)_d\) and are exactly the rows used by the artifact’s `lower=[2,2,0,0,0,0]`, `upper=[5,5,5,5,5,5]`, `hDegrees=[1,2,3,4,5]` construction.
## Strategy
Let \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\). Since \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\) and \(h_t=s_{(t)}\in I_{6,5}\) for \(t>5\),
\[
A_+=(\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_5).
\]
Using truncated LR multiplication [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 263-269], \(J\) is an ideal, and degreewise
\[
(A_+J)_d
=\sum_{t=1}^{5}\sum_{\substack{22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6\\|\lambda|=d-t}}
\mathbb Z\,\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda .
\]
Thus the complete indexed Pieri rows are precisely those labeled by
\[
R_d=\{(t,\lambda):1\le t\le5,\ 22\subseteq\lambda\subseteq5^6,\ |\lambda|=d-t\},
\]
with coordinates
\[
\bar h_t\bar s_\lambda
=\sum_{\substack{\nu\subseteq5^6\\\nu/\lambda\text{ horizontal }t\text{-strip}}}\bar s_\nu .
\]
This agrees with the intended construction recorded for artifact
`a3ad933b835c991bc8edccec918dce17c0e4594e4d1d4281e32946dd7e508ece`
in its computed degrees \(4,\ldots,30\).

## Gaps
The literal all-degree artifact claim is not established. Indeed, \(J_d=0\) for \(d>30\), but \(R_d\) is nonempty for every \(5\le d\le35\). For \(31\le d\le35\), \((d-30,5^6)\in R_d\), and every such row is the zero row because its target lies in \(J_d=0\). The recorded artifact was executed only in degrees \(4,\ldots,30\), hence does not literally contain these nonempty indexed zero-row families.

For precision, \(R_d=\varnothing\) for \(d\le4\) and \(d>35\); it is nonempty for \(5\le d\le35\). Thus equality of row lattices outside degree \(30\) does not yield equality of complete indexed row sets.

## Next
Extend the same construction through degree \(35\), preserving the zero-row labels in degrees \(31,\ldots,35\). Until then, this certificate is **not established as written**.
